1  NC: 2024:KHC:42111  CRL.P No. 9977 of 2022  THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S 482 CR.PC PRAYING TO QUASH THE FINAL REPORT C.C.NO28206/2022 DATED 02.08.2022, FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 420 OF IPC AND 63 AND 65 OF COPYRIGHT ACT WHICH IS ON THE FILE OF IX ADDL.C.M.M COURT AT BENGALURU. 
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER Petitioner being accused No.1 in Crime No.4/2022 of Sampigehalli Police Station, now pending in C.C.No.28206/2022 on the file of the learned IX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (for short "IPC")
and under Sections 63 and 65 of Copyrights Act, 1957 (for short "Copyright Act") is seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him. 
2. Heard Sri. Edmond Dandy, learned counsel for the petitioner, Smt. Rashmi Jadhav, learned Additional SPP for respondent No.1, Smt. Varalakshmi Shet K. and Sri. Vinayak Kamath K for respondent No.2. Perused the material on record. 
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1. He is the owner of M/s.
NC: 2024:KHC:42111 Royal Acqua Industries, a start up company manufacturing the beverage by name "Royal Fizz Jeera Masala". Even though the petitioner is not a registered copy right holder, he is registered under Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (for short "the said Act of 2006") and accordingly, he is manufacturing and marketing the beverage after getting permission from the Food Safety and Security Authority of India (FSSAI). There is no violation of any of the provisions of the Copyright Act and therefore, the petition is liable to be allowed. 
4. Learned counsel also submitted that respondent No.2 has filed an application seeking to withdraw the complaint filed by it, inspite of that the Trial Court proceeded with the matter and on that count also, the criminal proceedings is liable to be quashed. Accordingly, prays for allowing the petition. 
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 while opposing the petition submitted that respondent No.2 is the registered copy right owner of the artistic work. He is running M/s. Megha Sri G Sandeep Reddy vs State Of Karnataka on 21 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12222052/
2 Fruits Processing Private Limited and producing beverage under the name and style as "Bindu Fizz Jeera Masala". The petitioner, who has started his business in the year 2018, copied NC:
2024:KHC:42111 the artistic work of respondent No.2 and thereby committed an offence as stated above. Even though respondent No.2 was ready to withdraw the complaint that was subject to the undertaking to be given by the present petitioner not to use the registered artistic work of respondent No.2, under such circumstances, the petition is liable to be dismissed. Accordingly,
prays for dismissal of the petition. 
6. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner made out any grounds for allowing the petition and to quash the FIR registered against him? 
My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 7. Respondent No.2, as informant filed first information against the petitioner and accused No.2 for the offences punishable under Section 420 IPC and under Sections 63 and 65 of the Copyright Act. 
The specific allegations made by respondent NC: 2024:KHC:42111 No.2 against the accused is that they started a company under the name and style as "Royal Aqua Industries Private Limited" and were marketing a beverage under the name and style as "Royal Fizz Jeera Masala". For marketing the said product, the registered artistic work of respondent No.2 is being used by them and thereby,
they have violated the provisions of Copyright Act and committed cheating. 
8. Admittedly, accused No.2 being owner of "Royal Aqua Industries Limited", a startup company,
began its business in the year 2018. It is stated that respondent No.2 has started its business during 2009 and it is the owner of the registered artistic work under the Copyright Act. The specific allegations are made against the accused regarding copying the registered artistic work and violating the provisions of Copyright Act and also committed cheating. It is for the Trial Court to come to the conclusion about the disputed facts of the case. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that respondent No.2 is not a registered copyright owner of the artistic work cannot be accepted at this stage, as it is a disputed fact. The complainant has asserted while filing the complaint that it is the owner of the registered copyright NC: 2024:KHC:42111 regarding the artistic work "Bindu Fizz Jeera Masala". Under such, circumstances, I am of the opinion that it is not a fit case for quashing the criminal proceedings. 
9. Learned counsel for the petitioner, at this stage, submits that the complainant has not came forward before the Trial Court to prosecute the proceedings. If that is so, the petitioner may request the Trial Court to pass appropriate orders and the same cannot be a ground to quash the criminal proceedings. Accordingly, I answer the above point in negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is dismissed.
